description: How often does the same ligand carry BOTH an active and an inactive label in MetalCytoToxDB, as a function of how many measurements it has? A label that were a deterministic property of the ligand would become MORE consistent with more measurements. It becomes less consistent.
source: molmetal/data/cytotox.py via MetalCytotoxDataset.from_csv, 5 metals, CytotoxFilter(time_threshold=24.0, ic50_min=0.01)

symmetric_flip_model.note: The model under-predicts at n=5 (0.281 vs 0.395), so the independent-per-measurement-noise story is directionally supported but NOT a good quantitative fit. Treat p as an order-of-magnitude estimate only.

implication_CORRECTED.what_is_solid: Contradiction rate rises monotonically from 0.141 at n=2 to 0.395 at n=5 — the qualitative conclusion (labels carry per-measurement noise, not a deterministic ligand property) is well supported by 58/95/71/49 contradictory groups.
implication_CORRECTED.what_is_NOT_solid: An earlier draft of todo.json asserted a 'Bayes accuracy ceiling of ~92%'. That number is 1-p, the probability that a SINGLE measurement is correct — it is not a ceiling on achievable AUC, and no such ceiling follows from a symmetric flip model (majority vote over repeated measurements converges to the true label). DO NOT quote a Bayes ceiling derived from this table.
implication_CORRECTED.correct_statement: Label noise attenuates the observed within-metal AUC relative to the underlying chemistry, and part of the gap to 1.0 is irreducible. The size of that part is not quantified here.
